context_for_next_testing_agent: Rider rule = seated shape (person box h/w < 1.8) moving faster than 1.5 body-heights/s is treated as a rider and suppressed from Person alerts; tall persons (h/w >= 1.8) count even when running; slow seated persons still count (walker). In this 2-CPU container 3-5 concurrent file-backed cameras produce fps ~2 and level 'bad'/'warn' — expected, not a bug.
rca of the issue: (A) 12:09 PM '2 persons' bug: YOLO drew the bike and the rider as two 'person' boxes without a motorcycle box, so the old rider suppression (which required a two-wheeler track with overlapping person) never fired. Fix verified: Track.label vote relabels a 'person' track to motorcycle/bicycle once >=25% of its detections were two-wheeler (test_iter34 scenario 4/4b), and engine._with_vehicle() now looks at the person's own shape and velocity — seated (h/w < 1.8) + fast (>1.5 heights/s) is treated as a rider even when no vehicle track is present (test_iter34 scenario 1). Walkers at walking speed (scenario 2), running tall persons (scenario 3), stocky slow walkers and group crossings (scenario 5) all still count. (B) Load Meter: backend adds a 1-Hz psutil sampler thread + per-camera 2-s fps/drop_pct window inside Worker._stream_once; _camera_load() thresholds (fps<4 or ai_ms>400=bad, fps<8 or ai_ms>250=warn) feed state['cameras'][].load and state['load'] with a Hinglish hint naming the slow cameras. Verified end-to-end via UI, API, and the multicam harness.
